title: Electric Field and Electron Beam Control of Atomic Motion in Rutile TiO2 by In-situ TEM
content: The ability to control atomic-scale material migration is crucial for advancing nanoelectronic devices. Understanding how external fields influence atomic motion in semiconducting thin films is essential for optimizing material synthesis and enhancing device reliability. However, directly imaging such migration under applied fields in semiconducting thin films remains challenging. In our previous work, we observed electron-beam-induced radiolysis-driven crack healing in rutile TiO2 [1] and demonstrated that applied voltages can control both the direction and rate of octahedral unit migration [2]. Based on these results, this study employs in-situ scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) with electrical biasing to further investigate how crack location and local electric field distribution influences materials restructuring.
